task.description:
Design the fix for ISS-0279 per ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis in handoffs/WF03-ISS0279-20260822/step-01-issue-fixer.json result.summary (read it in full -- it is your primary spec). Two surfaces: (1) doc/protocol wording upgrades to docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 and docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md making it a stated HARD requirement that any issue close (gh issue close, or a local status flip to resolved/no_defect/instrumented) must carry either a resolving --comment or a genuinely linked/merged PR with a Closes/Fixes reference; (2) a new Mix.Task, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex, modeled structurally on lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex (read it for the pattern: grandfather-list of pre-existing violations, exit non-zero only on NEW un-grandfathered violations, clear stdout report). It queries gh (issue list/view) for issues referenced by docs/issues/*.yaml github_issue fields, and flags any CLOSED issue with zero comments AND no linked/merged PR reference. You MUST resolve the open design question ISSUE-FIXER flagged and left unresolved: whether this tool assumes live GitHub network access (this repo has no .github/workflows and no CI network precedent -- mix letflow.check is the CI-substitute per ISS-0257) -- decide and document explicitly whether it (a) requires `gh` CLI + live network and is therefore documented as a LOCAL/ON-DEMAND-ONLY check (not silently assumed to run in a sandboxed/offline agent environment -- state this plainly so ELIXIR-DEV and REVIEWER don't wire it into a hard gate that will spuriously fail with no network), or (b) some other shape (e.g. reads a locally cached JSON export). Given ISS-0257's own precedent of wiring lint_handoffs into `letflow.check` as a hard gate, decide explicitly whether THIS tool should also be wired into `letflow.check` now, or left as a standalone `mix letflow.audit_issue_closures` invoked manually/periodically -- your design must state the rationale either way (a network-dependent tool folded unconditionally into a gate that must pass without network access would break the existing check alias for every offline run, so the default lean should be standalone unless you find a reason to run it conditionally/gracefully-skip-when-gh-unavailable). Write a design artefact to lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md covering: the exact new/changed prose for both docs, the audit tool's @moduledoc, its CLI invocation shape, its data flow (how it enumerates docs/issues/*.yaml, what gh command(s) it runs, exact JSON fields consulted), its grandfather-list format (mirror lint_handoffs's own format precisely), its exit-code/violation-report format, and how ELIXIR-DEV should populate the initial grandfather list (a fresh scan is out of scope for design -- direct ELIXIR-DEV to run the real audit once implemented and grandfather whatever pre-existing violations it finds, explicitly excluding GH#324 and GH#326 which are already resolved by WF03-ISS0278-20260822 and must NOT be grandfathered as violations if they now carry evidence). No implementation code -- design only (interfaces/specs/data shapes/CLI flags/exact doc prose), per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria. Complete this handoff: status PASS, artifacts_out listing the design doc path, next_action 'Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'. Claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED this design (handoffs/WF03-ISS0279-20260822/step-02b-code-design-validator.json) on AC6 (no implementation code) only -- 5 of 6 acceptance criteria passed cleanly and do not need to change. Fix required: section 2.5 of lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md contains a complete, working one-line function body (`defp grandfathered?(number), do: Enum.any?(@grandfathered, fn {n, _, _} -> n == number end)`) instead of a bare @spec. Strip that down to its @spec line only (e.g. `@spec grandfathered?(pos_integer()) :: boolean()` with a one-sentence prose description of what it does, no executable code). Also non-blocking but worth keeping: the validator noted the @grandfathered tuple shape ({issue_number, date, note}) differs from lint_handoffs.ex's real {rule, path} 2-tuple convention -- this is fine as-is, the design's existing justification (one hard rule vs. several, still per-item/dated/traced/no-wildcards) should be kept, do not revert to a literal copy of lint_handoffs's shape. This is not a first dispatch -- the handoff is already claimed and has a real result on it from the prior attempt. Flip status to COMPLETED (or FAILED) as normal on finishing, exactly as usual.
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md exists and covers both fix surfaces
Exact new/upgraded prose specified for WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 and ISSUE_QUEUE.md making evidence-on-close a hard requirement
letflow.audit_issue_closures Mix.Task design: @moduledoc, CLI shape, gh command(s) and JSON fields used, grandfather-list format (matching lint_handoffs's own convention), exit-code/report format
The live-GitHub-network-in-CI open question is explicitly resolved with stated rationale, not left open

No implementation code in the design artefact

result.summary: Design artefact written to lib/letflow/design/iss0279-issue-closure-audit.md covering both fix surfaces per the handoff brief. (1) DOC PROSE: exact replacement wording for WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 point 2 (evidence-on-close stated as a HARD requirement -- comment or genuinely linked/merged PR, GH#324/#326 cited as the concrete cost of skipping it) plus one added sentence after Step 5's output paragraph; and a new ISSUE_QUEUE.md section 'Closing an issue's GitHub mirror -- evidence is mandatory' (currently that file only covers filing, not closing) restating the same rule and pointing at the new audit tool. (2) TOOL DESIGN: mix letflow.audit_issue_closures (Mix.Tasks.Letflow.AuditIssueClosures), modeled structurally on letflow.lint_handoffs.ex -- full @moduledoc text, zero-arg CLI shape, data flow (docs/issues/*.yaml discovery via File.read!+Regex, matching check_requirements_registration.ex's existing convention since this project has no YAML-parsing dependency; one `gh issue view <n> --json number,state,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences` call per tracked issue; Jason decode), grandfather-list format ({issue_number, date, note} tuples, mirroring lint_handoffs's per-item no-blanket-suppression convention but simplified since there is only one hard rule, ZERO_EVIDENCE), and exact exit-code/report format (three-section stdout report, FETCH ERRORS forces non-zero distinctly from violations, OK line on a clean run). Section 2.6 directs ELIXIR-DEV to run the real audit once implemented and populate @grandfathered from actual findings, explicitly excluding GH#324/GH#326 (already resolved with real evidence by WF03-ISS0278-20260822, must not be grandfathered as if still violating). BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS RESOLVED (not left open): Q1 (live-GitHub-network) resolved as (a) -- the tool requires gh CLI + live network and is documented plainly as LOCAL/ON-DEMAND-ONLY, never assumed to run in a sandboxed/offline environment; rationale: repo has no .github/workflows, mix letflow.check is the CI substitute per ISS-0257, and every step currently in that alias (check_toolchain, check_requirements_registration, check_deferral_staleness, lint_handoffs, format --check-formatted, compile --warnings-as-errors, check.test) reads only local filesystem/git state with zero network dependency -- confirmed by reading mix.exs's aliases/0 directly. Q2 (letflow.check wiring) resolved as NO -- stays standalone, not added to aliases/0, because folding a network-dependent step into an alias every agent runs (including sandboxed/offline) would make it spuriously fail for reasons unrelated to code correctness; a graceful-skip-when-gh-unavailable variant was explicitly considered and rejected too, since a hard gate that silently no-ops under an undetectable condition manufactures false confidence rather than an honest absence -- WF-03 Step 5's hardened prose is the forward gate, this tool is the periodic after-the-fact backstop. No implementation code included -- interfaces, @moduledoc prose, CLI shape, data shapes, exact doc prose, and grandfather/report formats only.
